entities.summary: Zamfir Constantin Arbore was a Bukovinian-born Romanian political activist originally active in the Russian Empire, also known for his work as an amateur historian, geographer and ethnographer. Arbore debuted in left-wing politics from early in life, gained an intimate knowledge of the Russian revolutionary milieu, and participated in both nihilist and Narodnik conspiracies. Self-exiled to Switzerland, he became a member of the International Workingmen's Association. Arbore was mostly active as an international anarchist and a disciple of Mikhail Bakunin, but eventually parted with the latter to create his independent group, the Revolutionary Community.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: As a key figure in the Russian revolutionary milieu and a disciple of Mikhail Bakunin, Zamfir Arbore's work contributed to the development of anarchist thought and influenced the creation of his independent group, the Revolutionary Community. His involvement with the International Workingmen's Association also underscores his role as an international anarchist.
